g.text: Mathematics and assumptions

text.style: font-size: 10px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: Companion to the nine picture strips · constructions and their added premises

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: Reading the pictures
Read each strip left to right; row numbers here count from the top. Black and green distinguish contributions. Orange
shows a result, transferred piece or rate as specified below. Grey shows a prior position or shift; arrows in the gutters
indicate reading order. Drawn geometry is a chosen representation. No background axes, physical observer at infinity, or
quantum amplitudes are required to read the pictures.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 1–2 · Comparison, composition and cancellation
Supply an oriented affine plane and comparison by translation. Tip-to-tail joining defines vector addition; following a
step by its reverse gives zero net displacement. WDP §§1.1–1.4 requires a declared comparison structure. Its §17.7
constructs signed histories after alternative formation and additive completion are admitted. Geometric reverse steps
illustrate cancellation; they do not prove every physical operation reversible. WDP §17.8 constructs g(a,b)=L(a)ᵀL(b) from
a supplied additive report L, with radical ker L; that pairing is observer-relative, not selected by bare difference.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 3 · A report can forget what the next move needs
Inputs ψ±=(3,±4)/5 have equal component-length reports (3/5,4/5). Apply the SAME orthogonal matrix U=((3,4),(−4,3))/5:
Uψ+=(1,0), Uψ−=(−7,−24)/25. The picture uses scale 1.5 throughout. Middle-panel grey is the old joined vector; orange is
the rotated vector; the last panel resolves it into components. Equal old reports give different new ones, so no report-
only update works for both. A supplied square report gives (9/25,16/25) initially and first outputs 1 versus 49/625. This
is not Born uniqueness, nor a failure of the l1 norm to retain signs. Sources: FQM §13.8; Proofs §§1.2–1.4.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 4–5 · Balance first; a quarter-turn as an added move
Redistribute lengths (3,1)→(2,2); both total 4. More generally zₖ₊₁=zₖ+d₀* jₖ preserves the vertex sum because each
internal edge contributes opposite signs. For a closed cycle γ, ⟨A+d₀λ,γ⟩=⟨A,γ⟩. These are balance and repair-invariance
identities, not Noether’s theorem (WDP §5.12). Row 5 supplies J(x,y)=(−y,x): J²=−I and J⁴=I. With an admitted rational
pairing g and g(Jx,y)=−g(x,Jy), WDP §17.9 derives the Q(i) action (a+ib)x=ax+bJx and Hermitian form h=g+i g(J·,·). J and
its compatibility are inputs. Four quarter-turns give only four positions. Admitting ALL rational turns adds Q/Z; its
completion in a supplied circle metric is R/Z, not the time line.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 6 · The extra structure for classical Hamilton
Now supply a STATE plane with dimensionless conjugate coordinates q,p and area ω=dq∧dp. The two triangles form a patch of
area 5.4; the shown shears preserve it. In rows 7–9 black is q, green is p; right/up are positive. Their right angle does
not derive conjugacy. Supply a time-independent C¹ vector field X(q,p)=(u,v): u=q̇ and v=ṗ are continuously
differentiable instantaneous rates. Assume its local flow preserves EVERY small oriented area. Then ∂q u+∂p v=0, so α=u
dp−v dq is closed. On a simply connected patch (no holes), α=dH gives q̇=Hₚ and ṗ=−Hq. H is local, unique up to a
constant. The sampled shears illustrate this hypothesis; they do not establish it for arbitrary flows.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 7 · A continuous rule makes the arrow turn
Choose H=(q²+p²)/2, hence q̇=p and ṗ=−q simultaneously. Both rate panels show (2.1,1.2); orange rate lengths are 1.2 and
2.1 on the same scale, not successive kicks. The last panel shows exact states at t=0,0.5,1: q(t)=q₀ cos t+p₀ sin t,
p(t)=p₀ cos t−q₀ sin t. It preserves H and ω. Smaller snapshots alone do not prove continuity or select a generator. This
clockwise oscillator uses −J from row 5; reversing the orientation is explicit.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 8–9 · A different rule, its symmetry, and the Noether charge
Switch to H=p²/2: Φt(q,p)=(q+tp,p). Translations Ta(q,p)=(q+a,p) preserve ω and H, and commute with Φt. Both orderings
start at (2,0.65), use a=1.5, t=1, and end at (4.15,0.65); grey means shift, orange means slide. Row 9 is the unshifted
run t=0,1,2. Translation pairs with ω to give dp, so its charge is p; ṗ=−Hq=0. For S=∫(pq̇−H)dt, independent interior
variations with δq=0 at endpoints give Hamilton’s equations. Constant translations preserve S and map endpoint data to
translated data. Noether conservation holds on stationary trajectories; equal marks alone do not prove it.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: The separate algebraic Hamiltonian route and remaining limits
WDP §19A.6 instead supplies the FULL algebra M_d(Q(i)), its conjugate-linear adjoint, and a Q(i)-linear map δ with
δ(AB)=δ(A)B+Aδ(B) and δ(A†)=δ(A)†. S=Σⱼδ(Eⱼ₁)E₁ⱼ gives δ=[S,·]. Replace S by (S−S†)/2; H₀=iS then satisfies H₀†=H₀ and
δ=−i[H₀,·], unique modulo rational scalar identity. This constructs an algebraic generator, not a clock or flow, and is
distinct from row 6’s classical theorem. Neither route selects physical energy from marks. The sheets do not derive the
Born rule, Everett, Bell, a unique Hilbert geometry or physical laws. Novice comprehension remains untested.
